note: US House/Senate midterm races had not been officially called as of this run's verified clock (07:02 SGT Wed = ~18:02 ET Tue Nov 3); item 4 reflects pre-close prediction-market pricing, not a confirmed result.

items.headline: Nasdaq 100 officially enters correction (-10% from Oct 6 high); rout hit Asia chips hardest before a Tuesday US rebound
items.summary: Chip/memory stocks have shed roughly $3.7T in value since Oct 6. Korea bore the brunt Monday-Tuesday: Kospi fell 3.6% to 5,649 (Samsung -4.15%, SK Hynix -5.03%) and Taiwan's benchmark fell 3.6%, before US chips rebounded Tuesday (Nasdaq +0.83%, AMD +7% after-hours on data-center revenue +97%).
items.actionable: SMIC (0981) carries more direct AI-capex-doubt beta than Tencent/Xiaomi -- expect choppier, higher-amplitude swings in 0981 specifically on US chip-sector headlines over the next week.

items.headline: Gold/silver swept into the AI-stock deleveraging rather than trading as a clean safe-haven
items.summary: Gold hit a one-year low of $3,880.97 on Fri Oct 31 in forced-liquidation selling tied to the AI/chip rout, rebounded to ~$3,954 Nov 2, then eased to $3,940.20 (-0.74%) Nov 3. Silver broke below $50, rallied Nov 2, then eased to $49.81 (-1.79%) Nov 3. Analysts note gold is currently trading as a liquidity source for margin calls, not purely as a hedge.
items.actionable: The levered silver/miners book should expect correlation to equity drawdowns (margin-driven air pockets) right now, not clean safe-haven diversification -- size positions assuming metals can gap down with tech, not against it.

items.headline: RBA hikes to 4.85% -- 5th hike of 2026, highest since 2008, but on a 6-3 split vote citing oil/Mideast inflation
items.summary: The RBA raised its cash rate 25bp to 4.85%, with the board now not seeing inflation fall below 3% until late 2027 and explicitly citing Middle East conflict and oil-driven price pressure. The 6-3 vote split was wider than the near-unanimous economist call implied, and AUD fell below US$0.70.
items.actionable: Reinforces a higher-for-longer DM-rates regime that argues for keeping the large cash pile in short-duration rather than chasing duration-sensitive SGX REITs; a softer AUD is a modest cost tailwind for AUD-cost rare-earth miners Lynas/Iluka if it persists.

items.headline: US midterm elections: polls closed, counting underway -- no official calls yet, but election-day trading already pricing a likely Democratic House
items.summary: Pre-close prediction markets (Kalshi) gave Democrats roughly 93% odds on the House and 71% on the Senate; the Dow fell 0.38% while the S&P (+0.36%) and Nasdaq (+0.83%) rose on election day itself. CNBC separately flagged a real risk of Trump contesting results, which could create a prolonged period of market uncertainty.
items.actionable: Treat any post-election 'gridlock relief' rally as fragile given the contested-results risk CNBC flagged -- don't chase a knee-jerk bounce in HK tech/REITs until House/Senate are actually called.

items.headline: China's 0.1%-threshold rare-earth export-control truce expires Nov 10 with no public renewal signal
items.summary: The one-year suspension of China's harshest extraterritorial rare-earth licensing rule (anything with 0.1%+ Chinese-origin rare-earth content needs Beijing sign-off) lapses Nov 10; Beijing has given no public signal on renewal, narrowing, or termination. The IEA estimates $6.5T of downstream Western auto/chip/defense output is exposed if it is not renewed.
items.actionable: This is the single highest-conviction near-term catalyst for the rare-earths watchlist -- Nov 10 is 6 days away; consider pre-positioning or at least setting alerts, since a lapse (vs. a quiet extension matching the broader US-China truce to Jan 10, 2027) would be a sharp divergence trade.

items.headline: MP Materials down ~60% from highs on concerns earnings are Pentagon-subsidy-dependent; reports Q3 Nov 5
items.summary: MP Materials has fallen roughly 60% from its October 2025 highs, with over 60% of last quarter's adjusted EBITDA ($17.6M) coming from Pentagon price-floor payments rather than organic profitability. Short interest is 20.35% of float as of Nov 3, and the stock reports Q3 earnings Nov 5.
items.actionable: Nov 5 is a binary-ish event for MP given elevated short interest and the subsidy-dependency debate -- treat MP as the highest-volatility name in the watchlist into that print.

items.headline: Lynas signs $96M, 4-year Pentagon deal matching MP Materials' $110/kg NdPr price floor
items.summary: Lynas (LYC.AX), the largest rare-earth producer outside China, secured a DoD deal for light and heavy rare-earth oxides with a $110/kg NdPr price floor -- mirroring the floor the Pentagon already gives MP Materials.
items.actionable: Validates the 'Pentagon price floor' de-risking thesis now extending beyond MP to Lynas -- supportive for the watchlist's downside protection narrative even if the China truce lapses.

items.headline: Critical-minerals complex sells off on dilution jitters: Critical Metals -11%, USA Rare Earth -10%, MP Materials -6%
items.summary: A European lithium-deal-related share issuance spooked the broader critical-minerals sector, with Critical Metals falling 11%, USA Rare Earth 10%, and MP Materials 6% in sympathy.
items.actionable: Shows the whole junior rare-earth complex is prone to sympathy selloffs on financing/dilution news anywhere in the sector -- a risk distinct from the China-truce catalyst above.

items.headline: JL MAG (6680.HK) Q3 revenue +56% YoY, 9-month profit guided +43-55% YoY, dividend payable ~Nov 20
items.summary: JL MAG's Q3 revenue rose 56% YoY despite weak downstream EV demand; nine-month net profit guided up 43-55% YoY. Board approved Q3 results Oct 27; interim dividend payable around Nov 20.
items.actionable: Strong, policy-tailwind-independent fundamentals here (unlike MP's subsidy dependency) -- JL MAG is arguably the cleanest 'pure rare-earth-magnet demand growth' expression in the watchlist right now.

items.headline: Xiaomi October EV deliveries top 50,000 for the first time, 61% of full-year target hit
items.summary: Xiaomi delivered more than 50,000 EVs in October, its highest monthly level this year, bringing 10-month cumulative deliveries to roughly 336,490 against a 550,000 full-year target.
items.actionable: A genuine fundamental positive for Xiaomi distinct from the HK-tech sentiment/chip-correlation noise -- supports holding through the broader Asia tech volatility described above.

items.headline: Oil stabilizes after Monday's crash; Iran reiterates Hormuz stays closed, complicating the 'reopening' narrative
items.summary: Brent closed -0.33% to $104.42 and WTI +0.31% to $96.76 Tuesday, largely flat after Monday's double-digit crash on Iran-US diplomacy hopes. But Iran stated the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed unless Washington meets its conditions, while Trump claimed the US has 'total control' of the waterway.
items.actionable: The oil-crash thesis is not yet confirmed by an actual Hormuz reopening -- keep the inflation/Fed-hawkish read conditional, don't treat the de-escalation as settled.

items.headline: S-REITs down 8.2% YTD vs. STI +24.6% as firming Dec-hike odds remove near-term REIT relief
items.summary: DBS/OCBC/UOB (over half of STI weight) posted record H1 profits and have driven the STI's 24.6% YTD gain, while the S-REIT index is down 8.2% YTD. Fed-funds pricing now puts December-hike odds near 73%, removing a tailwind S-REITs would need to re-rate.
items.actionable: The bank-vs-REIT dispersion in the SGX book looks likely to persist or widen given the hawkish December Fed pricing -- favor the banks over REITs into year-end unless SORA eases faster than US rates.

items.headline: Hecla Mining reports Q3 2026 results today, emphasizing record production and a debt-free balance sheet
items.summary: Hecla holds its Q3 earnings call this morning US time (10am EST), with pre-release framing emphasizing record production and a debt-free balance sheet amid North American silver-mine expansion.
items.actionable: First concrete silver-mining data point of the week -- watch for guidance commentary on cost inflation/expansion that could set the tone for the levered silver-miner names in the book today.
